trust_decision.summary: Whether the request's `redirect` query parameter is safe to hand to the application's redirect is decided once, in AuthenticationService::getLoginRedirect(): it parses the value, rejects any scheme or host, makes the path root-relative and returns it. The published fix adds WHATWG-style backslash normalisation at that same decision, because browsers rewrite `\` to `/` in the Location header, so `/\evil.com` passed the host/scheme check as a plain path and then resolved to `//evil.com` off-site.

landing_point.why: An engineer who read only 'open redirect weakness via backslash bypass in getLoginRedirect()' opens the single parse_url() call on the redirect query parameter. That line is where all three public entry points converge: AuthenticationService::getLoginRedirect() (src/AuthenticationService.php:390, declared on the contract at src/AuthenticationServiceInterface.php:86), AuthenticationComponent::getLoginRedirect() (src/Controller/Component/AuthenticationComponent.php:365) and AuthenticationComponent::redirectAfterLogin() (src/Controller/Component/AuthenticationComponent.php:385).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The component methods are documented as convenience wrappers over the plugin's already-validated service method (docs/en/authentication-component.md:142-151, docs/en/authenticators.md:580-603), so a solver can argue that AuthenticationService::getLoginRedirect() is the only place that needs the check and that the component wrappers at src/Controller/Component/AuthenticationComponent.php:371 and :387 inherit it for free - which is in fact true here.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Root-relativising a target that has no leading slash must keep working: 'ok.com/path' must still come back as '/ok.com/path', and a single leading backslash '\evil.com/path' must still come back as '/evil.com/path' (the fix keeps this deliberately). redirectAfterLogin() must still emit a Location for such relative targets. A fix that rejects every value containing a backslash, or every value not starting with '/', breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: absolute URL with scheme and host (http://evil.ca/evil/path) - rejected by the pre-existing host/scheme check
protocol-relative with forward slashes (//evil.com/path) - rejected (new explicit leading-'//' check plus the old host check)
protocol-relative spelled with backslashes (\\evil.com/path) - normalised to //evil.com/path and rejected
mixed separators (/\evil.com, \/\evil.com) - normalised to ///evil.com and /////evil.com and rejected
single leading backslash ('\evil.com/path') - normalised to /evil.com/path and still allowed
relative path without a leading slash ('ok.com/path') - leading '/' is added
path carrying a query string ('/path/with?query=string', '/articles/index?sort=created&direction=desc') - preserved
non-string query value cast with (string) (an array param becomes 'Array')

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a redirectAfterLogin() that reads the redirect query parameter from the controller request itself and passes it to Controller::redirect() instead of delegating to getLoginRedirect()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the newer post-login convenience helper, documented as using 'the plugin's validated login redirect target' (docs/en/authentication-component.md:127-143); a maintainer could plausibly have written it self-contained. The real code delegates at :387-389, so a planted copy would only be a where-type sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same backslash and leading-'//' guard inside getUnauthenticatedRedirectUrl(), which already serialises the blocked request path into the login URL's redirect parameter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That method performs the same parse_url() plus path reassembly pattern (src/AuthenticationService.php:369-378) and produces the value getLoginRedirect later validates, so a maintainer sanitising at the producer could reasonably add the guard there as well.

O9_family: URL redirection to untrusted site (CWE-601, open redirect)

O10_build.toolchain: composer + PHPUnit (php >= 8.1, cakephp/http ^5.0, laminas-diactoros ^3.0); CI reuses cakephp/.github testsuite-without-db
O10_build.project_tests: tests/TestCase/AuthenticationServiceTest.php: testGetLoginRedirect at :825 and the redirect-validation tests at :868-1026; tests/TestCase/Controller/Component/AuthenticationComponentTest.php: testGetLoginRedirect at :369, testRedirectAfterLogin at :405 and the absolute / protocol-relative fallback tests at :433-476

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject any redirect value that contains a backslash (or that does not start with '/'), which also kills the legitimate '\evil.com/path' -> '/evil.com/path' and 'ok.com/path' -> '/ok.com/path' conversions the tests require.

out_of_scope_notes: CakePHP core's Controller::redirect() / Router::normalize() handling of backslash targets lives in cakephp/cakephp, outside this repository, and was not examined.
unverified: repo_mb was not measured (no shell in this session); the tree has 144 tracked files and no vendor/ or node_modules/ directory, so tiny_repo is an estimate from the file inventory rather than a measurement.

Which branch each of the three fix commits targets could not be checked (no shell); src/AuthenticationService.php at the pinned commit matches the pre-image of ee24bd48 exactly, and the five redirect-validation test methods added by 1c1e29c already exist verbatim at tests/TestCase/AuthenticationServiceTest.php:868-1026. I judged them pre-existing tests of the same area (the redirectValidation feature is already in the pinned src at :431-460, and they contain no backslash assertions), so regression_tests_in_pinned_commit was not raised.

Whether the fixed check still lets a tab/newline variant through (WHATWG strips those before parsing, while the patch only rewrites backslashes) was not exercised - no code was run. If true it is a residual bypass at the same site, not a separate route, so it is not listed in O8.
Whether Controller::redirect() in CakePHP core would itself normalise a backslash target on some other path was not checked (outside this repository).
